title: Against those who say the soul is harmony
pass_a_gloss: Against the claim that the soul is a harmony. Learning is recollection; if that is true, the soul is not a harmony of the body. Further, the soul also opposes the body and holds the ruler's place, whereas harmony does not rule the lyre. Harmony is an accident of tuned parts and admits more and less; the soul does not become more or less soul. Harmony perishes when the instrument is destroyed; the soul is not destroyed with the body's broken tuning. Therefore the soul is not harmony. Plato's solutions in the Phaedo are to be set out against the lyre comparison.
pass_b_english: Some say the soul is only a tuning — a harmony of the body. But if learning is recollection, the soul must already be something before this body's tuning. The soul can resist the body and govern it; a harmony does not command the lyre. Harmony grows tighter or looser; soul does not become more or less soul. Break the instrument and the tuning is gone; the soul is not dismissed with a broken frame. So the soul is not harmony. The lyre image meets the answers already given in Plato's Phaedo.
